title: Enterprise Complaint Intelligence
businessProblem: Customer complaints were manually categorized, slowing response times and increasing operational effort.

challenges: Inconsistent complaint labels across channels.
High volume of incoming requests with manual review.
Need for reliable category mapping without exposing internal data.
Real-time routing expectations for operational teams.
solution: Designed an enterprise intent classification platform using Generative AI to automate complaint categorization and routing.
responsibilities: Defined the AI solution architecture and deployment model.
Built prompt-guided classification pipelines for company-specific complaint categories.
Integrated output with downstream workflows for triage and escalation.
Validated impact against service-level requirements and business KPIs.
impact: 80% reduction in manual categorization effort.
Improved routing accuracy for complaint handling.
Faster customer resolution through automatic triage.
lessons: Business-aligned classification delivers more value than generic intent models.
Data quality and taxonomy design are the foundation of reliable automation.
Experimenting with lightweight prompts enabled fast iteration without model retraining.

title: Enterprise RAG Knowledge Assistant
businessProblem: Enterprise teams spent hours manually searching contracts, policies, technical documentation, and knowledge repositories, slowing decision-making and increasing dependency on subject matter experts.
businessContext: The organization required an intelligent knowledge retrieval platform that could answer natural language questions using enterprise documents while maintaining high accuracy and minimizing AI hallucinations.
challenges: Large volumes of unstructured documents across multiple formats.
Balancing retrieval accuracy with low response latency.
Reducing hallucinations by grounding responses in enterprise knowledge.
Designing a scalable architecture capable of handling continuous document growth.
solution: Designed and developed a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform that combined semantic search, vector embeddings, intelligent document chunking, and Large Language Models to deliver accurate, context-aware answers from enterprise documents.
responsibilities: Designed the end-to-end RAG architecture and document ingestion pipeline.
Implemented document preprocessing, chunking, embedding generation, and semantic retrieval workflows.
Optimized prompt engineering and retrieval strategies to improve answer quality.
Developed backend APIs and collaborated with stakeholders to validate response accuracy and business value.
impact: Reduced enterprise document lookup from 5+ days to minutes.
Accelerated business decision-making through faster knowledge retrieval.
Improved accessibility of enterprise knowledge across business teams.
Reduced dependency on subject matter experts for routine information requests.
lessons: High-quality retrieval has a greater impact on response quality than prompt complexity alone.
Well-designed document chunking and metadata significantly improve semantic search performance.
Grounding LLM responses with retrieved context increases user trust and reduces hallucinations.
